Another option could be to store the timestamp of the last check on a checkpoint file (/var/lib/kubelet/...).
In normal operation this checkpoint would be ignored,because kubelet can keep the necessary state in memory, but on kubelet restart/node reboot this will give us a way to do a precise recovery.
Additionally, if the checkpoint is missing, kubelet can happily keep its current behavior (either the one fixed in this PR or the previous).
I'm not sure the extra complexity is worht the gains, and I'm not approver so I can't really say, but I for myself would explore this way.

there is a data race,but not occured panic,the root case as i say FakeRuntime shared a variable to caller,so there maybe write and read at the same time.
Even if used lock in `GetImageRef` and `ListImages`,but when the caller get the result of `ListImages`, caller can write it without lock,this operate is out the range of `FakeRuntime`.
I still think we can use snapshot to fix this,if use lock we need coupling the manager and runtime.
```go
func (f *FakeRuntime) GetImageRef(_ context.Context, image kubecontainer.ImageSpec) (string, error) {
	f.Lock()
	defer f.Unlock()

	f.CalledFunctions = append(f.CalledFunctions, "GetImageRef")
	for _, i := range f.ImageList {
		if i.ID == image.Image {
			return i.ID, nil
		}
	}
	return "", f.InspectErr
}

func (f *FakeRuntime) ListImages(_ context.Context) ([]kubecontainer.Image, error) {
	f.Lock()
	defer f.Unlock()

	f.CalledFunctions = append(f.CalledFunctions, "ListImages")
	return f.ImageList, f.Err
}
```

issue_context.title: [kubelet-image-gc] minimum-image-ttl-duration not work,when kubelet restart.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

when kubelet restart,all images which notused cleaned.
but there is a flag in kubelet,`minimum-image-ttl-duration`,explain：Minimum age for an unused image before it is garbage collected.  Examples: '300ms', '10s' or '2h45m'.
i set `minimum-image-ttl-duration` to `20m0s`,it's means if a image not used,it will live 20m and then clean by kubelet（if has disk pressure）.if kubelet not restart, it work,but if restart ther is a bug, `minimum-image-ttl-duration` not work,image will be clean，even if it's no enough  time.


### What did you expect to happen?

`minimum-image-ttl-duration` work, image even if not used,it will live 20m and then clean by kubelet.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1）make node trigger disk pressure.
2）pull some image which not used by pod
3）restart kubelet
4）image cleaned by kubelet after around 10s

### Anything else we need to know?

i see the source code, and maybe there is a bug.

in [detectImages](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/kubelet/images/image_gc_manager.go#L261-L262) func,well detect image and update firstdetect time for every image.
```go
	// New image, set it as detected now.
		if _, ok := im.imageRecords[image.ID]; !ok {
			klog.V(5).InfoS("Image ID is new", "imageID", image.ID)
			im.imageRecords[image.ID] = &imageRecord{
				firstDetected: detectTime,
			}
		}
```
and in  [freeSpace](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/kubelet/images/image_gc_manager.go#L394C1-L397) func,well check images livetime by firstDetected.
```go
		if freeTime.Sub(image.firstDetected) < im.policy.MinAge {
			klog.V(5).InfoS("Image ID's age is less than the policy's minAge, not eligible for garbage collection", "imageID", image.id, "age", freeTime.Sub(image.firstDetected), "minAge", im.policy.MinAge)
			continue
		}
```
if kubelet running normal,it work,because there is a [Start](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/kubelet/images/image_gc_manager.go#L190-L204) func.
```go
func (im *realImageGCManager) Start() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	go wait.Until(func() {
		// Initial detection make detected time "unknown" in the past.
		var ts time.Time
		if im.initialized {
			ts = time.Now()
		}
                // in first time,ts is zero. 
               // in first time,ts is zero.
		_, err := im.detectImages(ctx, ts)
		if err != nil {
			klog.InfoS("Failed to monitor images", "err", err)
		} else {
			im.initialized = true
		}
	}, 5*time.Minute, wait.NeverStop)
//...

```
in this line,`_, err := im.detectImages(ctx, ts)`,in first time,ts is zero. so image's firstDetected time is zero,and in freeSpace
`reeTime.Sub(image.firstDetected) < im.policy.MinAge` this check is always false,so image will be cleaned.


maybe we can change to `im.detectImages(time.now())`,can fix this bug.

thinking about it, previously a kubelet restart triggered a GC (which is exactly what is being fixed here) and I wonder if there are ppl out there depending on this to free disk space on nodes with high disk pressure.
However now we need to wait a bit more (basically the actual min age to expire after a restart) so it should not be a big deal even for these folks.
